::: {.assignment-intro}
This group project compares listed companies in Australia and Malaysia from 2017 to 2021 using OSIRIS financial data. It builds a common analytical dataset, uses robust statistics to handle strongly skewed company ratios, and explores national, industry, and geographic patterns before, during, and after the initial COVID-19 shock.

## Key findings

- Malaysian firms showed more stable profitability, liquidity, and capital structure, with median EBITDA margins remaining positive through 2020.
- Australian firms displayed much wider variation and weaker median profitability, although some industries recovered as operating margins improved in 2021.
- Both countries remained relatively conservative in their use of leverage, while Malaysian firms showed higher median asset efficiency.
- Corporate activity clustered around major economic centres in both countries; location alone did not cleanly separate profitable from unprofitable firms.

The report combines data cleaning, missingness analysis, robust time-series summaries, industry comparisons, interactive charts, and spatial maps.
